transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-01 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Priya (Argo Head of Search), Tom (Argo ML), Sara (Argo Infra), Diego (PM)

[00:00] Jesse (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, this is jesse from redwood inference, with maya who is our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya (Argo): good thanks, excited to dig in. we've been looking at embeddings+rerank to improve our search relevance across product docs.
[00:12] Tom (Argo): hi all, quick background: we currently run open search + custom bm25, we do a candidate generation then a transformer-based rerank but it's slow and expensive.
[00:20] Maya (Redwood): got it. just so i understand scale, what's your corpus size and QPS right now?
[00:26] Priya: roughly 200k active docs, up to 1M in cold store. Peak QPS is ~120 qps across regions, typical 30-40 qps. rerank is sync on read today so p99 latency is bad.
[00:38] Jesse: and what's your current embedding strategy? are you using dense vectors for retrieval or only for rerank?
[00:42] Tom: we tried using openai embeddings for a PoC. vector DB is a mix — trialling pinecone and a local faiss service. dimensionality we experimented with 1536 and 768. 1536 gives better perf but costs more.
[00:55] Maya: makes sense. two common architectures: 1) hybrid search where you do bm25 or inverted index for candidate generation then vector rerank, 2) purely vector nearest neighbor with an HNSW index. both have tradeoffs for throughput and freshness.
[01:10] Priya: our freshness req is near real-time; docs update several times per hour and we need updates reflected within 30-60s ideally.
[01:16] Sara (Argo): security is also a hard constraint; we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS integration, and potentially VPC for the pilot.
[01:24] Maya: that's totally reasonable. Redwood Private supports on-prem and VPC with customer-managed KMS; Dedicated can also be in a VPC with private networking. Hosted API is simpler but you'd need to check data residency.
[01:35] Jesse: for a first pass many customers start hosted to validate qual then move to dedicated for predictable throughput and to control P95/P99 latency.
[01:43] Diego: can you give us rough numbers for embedding throughput and cost?
[01:47] Maya: rough ballpark: on Dedicated with 8x A100-equivalent GPUs you can get to several thousand embeddings per second if optimized batch size and async pipelines. For 1536-d vectors that impacts memory and indexing cost. Cost depends on commit and model — we'll share pricing.
[02:03] Tom: for rerank latencies we need sub-200ms for the reranker ideally, end-to-end under 500ms. is that feasible?
[02:11] Maya: with a lightweight rerank model or distilled reranker you can hit sub-200ms on dedicated inference nodes if you do batching carefully and use KV cache for chat-like workloads; for single-shot rerank it's more about concurrency.
[02:23] Jesse: also hybrid approach helps — bm25 candidate gen reduces nn-search cost, so reranker only runs on top N candidates (e.g., top 50).
[02:30] Priya: what about index updates with Faiss/HNSW? we can't rebuild a huge index every update.
[02:35] Maya: HNSW supports incremental inserts; Faiss has options too but it depends on the index type. For near-real-time we typically recommend an append-only shard strategy and background merges; Redwood can orchestrate index ingestion and incremental updates via our SDK or ingestion pipeline.
[02:50] Tom: do you host the vector DB or do we keep our own?
[02:54] Jesse: two patterns: 1) customers use managed vector DBs like Pinecone or Milvus + Redwood handles embeddings and rerank calls, 2) customers run Faiss/HNSW in their infra and call Redwood for embeddings + rerank inference. Both are common.
[03:06] Priya: when you say rerank are you talking about using redwood for the model scoring only, or also for embedding generation?
[03:11] Maya: both. we can generate embeddings in-hosted or dedicated and also host rerank models. Many customers keep vector indexes in their VPC and call Redwood Dedicated for large-batch embed generation and for low-latency reranking.
[03:22] Diego: how do you handle dimensionality tradeoffs? i.e., 512 vs 1536 vectors.
[03:25] Maya: lower dims reduce storage and speed up ANN; sometimes people do PCA or product quantization to get smaller footprint. There's a quality tradeoff — often 768 or 1024 is a good middle ground versus full 1536. Also model choice matters: some embedding models are 768 by default.
[03:40] Tom: what about hybrid search — combining bm25+embedding? any best practices?
[03:44] Maya: yes, do BM25 for recall, then vector rerank top-k. You can also score as a linear blend of bm25 score + cosine sim. For re-ranking we normalize scores and retrain a small ranker if needed.
[03:55] Priya: our infra team is worried about memory pressure for storing vectors plus production app. how do you recommend serving at scale?
[04:00] Maya: ways to mitigate: quantization (int8, 4-bit) for storage, sharding vectors across nodes, or using a hybrid approach where hot docs are cached in-memory, cold docs on disk. Redwood's Dedicated offers tunable capacity and autoscaling so you can size nodes for vector memory.
[04:15] Sara: any network bandwidth concerns? moving big batches of embeddings around can be heavy.
[04:18] Maya: yes, for high throughput you want to colocate embedding generation with index ingestion or use dedicated ingestion nodes. Batch upload APIs and compression help.
[04:25] Jesse: can i ask about benchmarks — do you have benchmarks for faiss vs pinecone vs dedicated redwood rerank?
[04:30] Maya: we have internal perf numbers and a public benchmark sheet we'll share; but results vary a lot with vector dim, QPS pattern, and candidate sizes. For raw latency, a tuned Faiss HSNW on local NVMe can be very fast. Managed systems trade off simplicity vs latency.
[04:45] Tom: in terms of security, we'll need SAML SSO, audit logs, and customer-managed KMS — are these available?
[04:51] Jesse: yes, Redwood Dedicated and Private support SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS integrations. we'll attach SOC2 attestation and compliance docs.
[04:59] Priya: on cost side, what's the typical pilot like? we want to prove quality before committing to large spend.
[05:03] Jesse: typical pilot: 2-4 week POC with 50-200k docs, run relevance evals (MRR, recall@k) and latency/cost benchmarking. Redwood provides temporary test capacity or a small dedicated cluster for pilots.
[05:15] Diego: how about model drift and monitoring?
[05:18] Maya: Redwood Optimize can monitor quality regressions vs baseline prompt sets; you can track embedding similarity drift and trigger re-indexing.
[05:26] Tom: any gotchas for updating vectors when you change embedding model? we fear full re-embedding costs.
[05:31] Maya: yes it's heavy. incremental strategies: 1) version vectors and serve hybrid indexes, 2) re-embed in background, 3) sample-based quality checks to detect needed full re-embeds. We'll include suggestions in the pilot plan.
[05:45] Priya: ok this is helpful. what's the decision timeline?
[05:48] Priya: we're aiming to pick a vendor for pilot by mid-march and have pilot run end of march.
[05:53] Jesse: sounds good. we'll send pricing + security docs and propose a benchmark test plan.
[05:58] Diego: one more question — can redwood run private deployment in our AWS account?
[06:02] Maya: yes, Redwood Private can be deployed in customer VPC or on-prem; Dedicated can also be set up with private networking. we'll need to coordinate infra access for the POC.
[06:12] Tom: for the benchmark, what metrics should we capture?
[06:15] Maya: capture latency p50/p95/p99, QPS, CPU/GPU utilization, embedding throughput (embeds/sec), recall@k, MRR, and storage costs per vector. Also track cold vs warm cache behaviors.
[06:28] Priya: do you provide retrain-ready logs for later analysis?
[06:31] Jesse: yes, we can export anonymized traces and token-level cost/latency breakdowns via the console.
[06:37] Sara: any network security checklist we should prepare?
[06:40] Maya: provide VPC peering details, proxy/firewall egress rules, and any IP allowlist; we'll share a checklist doc.
[06:46] Priya: ok last thing — what about multi-region search? our users are global.
[06:50] Maya: Redwood can route requests by region and replicate indexes or maintain regional shards; tradeoffs are consistency vs latency. We'll propose a regional pilot approach.
[07:01] Jesse: great recap — next steps are pricing + security docs, benchmark plan, and scheduling the technical deep dive. any final Qs?
[07:07] Priya: none here, thanks.
[07:09] Tom: thanks, bye.

Notes: transcript has occasional mis-hearings; some technical terms abbreviated. References: shared benchmark spreadsheet (link-to-bench), SOC2 doc (link-to-soc2), pilot proposal templ (link-to-proposal).
